$comment: App-size baseline for measure-nativeaot.mjs. Every number is a DELTA in bytes over the
gamebase row, never an absolute size, so it survives .NET SDK patch drift and runner
differences that absolute thresholds cannot.
The linux-x64 entry below was measured on a GitHub ubuntu-latest runner by the app-size job
in ci.yml (run 32603450209), which is the only place the repository publishes NativeAOT for
linux-x64. It replaces numbers transcribed from docs/guides/il2cpp-size-protocol.md §3 that
predated the runtime's current shape: every row measured 9-16 KB above them, so the advisory
warning fired on all eight rows and said nothing. Real numbers, so "gate": true — a byte
move outside the tolerance now fails the build.
Re-recorded from run 34060022503 (the round-3 runtime fixes: storage-class guard on the read
path, drain-until-empty loop, control-table shape snapshot, drained-row set). Those added a fixed
12.5 KB raw / 6 KB gz to every host-bearing row (8.3 KB raw on compact50-slim) — the intended
cost of four new failure modes, not a per-method regression: the marginal per-method costs
did not move.
Re-record after a change that is supposed to move bytes: read the app-size job's summary,
confirm the new numbers are what the change intended, then run
`UPDATE_SIZE_BASELINE=1 node tests/app-size-bench/measure-nativeaot.mjs --rid linux-x64`
on a runner and commit the rewritten file. Same regeneration idiom as UPDATE_DELIVERY_GOLDENS.
The shape invariants in measure-nativeaot.mjs (profile ordering, falling per-method cost,
H-FIELDS no-op, SLIM a net win, reflection-free build runs) are enforced regardless of this
gate — those are ratios, not bytes.
